question: Which in-stock PDUs state a 20 A rating?
reference_sql:
select m.name as manufacturer, p.manufacturer_part_number, p.rated_amps, p.in_stock_qty,
       p.lead_time_days, p.description
from parts p
join manufacturers m using (manufacturer_id)
where p.category = 'Power Outlet Strips'
  and p.rated_amps = 20
  and p.in_stock_qty > 0
order by p.in_stock_qty desc
correct_behavior: answer: list the in-stock power strips that state 20 A, with stock and lead time. Say this is the unit's stated rating, often its input, not the per-circuit breaker rating, so each datasheet must be checked.
source: golden_questions.md #1; db/queries.sql Q1; baseline: Vertiv 16 A vs 20 A

question: How many power strips state an amp rating at all?
reference_sql:
select coalesce(p.rated_amps::text, 'not stated') as rated_amps,
       count(*) as parts,
       count(*) filter (where p.in_stock_qty > 0) as in_stock,
       round(100.0 * count(*) / sum(count(*)) over (), 1) as pct_of_power_strips
from parts p
where p.category = 'Power Outlet Strips'
group by p.rated_amps
order by parts desc
correct_behavior: answer: give the count and share of power strips with no stated rating and the counts per stated rating. Say a filter on amps alone misses the strips that state none.
source: golden_questions.md #2; db/queries.sql Q2; baseline: Vertiv 16 A vs 20 A

question: How many commodity cables are in stock, and do out-of-stock ones have an ETA?
reference_sql:
with next_arrival as (
    select part_id, min(expected_date) as next_date
    from part_on_order
    where expected_date >= current_date
    group by part_id
)
select p.category,
       count(*) as parts,
       count(*) filter (where p.in_stock_qty > 0) as in_stock,
       count(*) filter (where p.in_stock_qty = 0) as out_of_stock,
       count(*) filter (where p.in_stock_qty = 0 and n.part_id is not null) as out_of_stock_with_eta,
       min(n.next_date) filter (where p.in_stock_qty = 0) as soonest_eta,
       count(*) filter (where p.in_stock_qty = 0 and p.lead_time_days = 0) as out_of_stock_lead_not_stated,
       round(avg(p.lead_time_days) filter (where p.in_stock_qty = 0 and p.lead_time_days > 0)) as avg_lead_days_when_stated
from parts p
left join next_arrival n using (part_id)
where p.category in ('Ethernet Cables / Networking Cables', 'Fiber Optic Cable Assemblies', 'AC Power Cords')
group by p.category
order by p.category
correct_behavior: answer: give in-stock and out-of-stock counts per cable category and how many out-of-stock parts have an on-order date. Say stock is as of the last sync.
source: golden_questions.md #4; db/queries.sql Q4; baseline: Commodity cables

question: Which manufacturer is cheapest for 100 Cat6A 3 ft cables, before and after the quoted tariff?
reference_sql:
with price_at_100 as (
    select distinct on (b.part_id) b.part_id, b.unit_price
    from price_breaks b
    where b.quantity <= 100
    order by b.part_id, b.quantity desc
)
select m.name as manufacturer,
       count(*) as parts,
       round(min(a.unit_price), 2) as cheapest_listed,
       round(min(a.unit_price * (1 + coalesce(p.tariff_pct, 0) / 100)), 2) as cheapest_with_tariff,
       max(p.tariff_pct) as highest_tariff_pct,
       max(p.in_stock_qty) as most_in_stock
from parts p
join manufacturers m using (manufacturer_id)
join price_at_100 a using (part_id)
where p.category = 'Ethernet Cables / Networking Cables'
  and p.description ~* 'cat\s*-?6a'
  and p.description ~* '\m3 ?(ft|foot)\M'
  and p.min_order_qty <= 100
group by m.name
order by cheapest_with_tariff
correct_behavior: answer: rank manufacturers by price at 100 both before and after the quoted tariff, and say whether 100 are in stock. Never rank on listed price alone.
source: golden_questions.md #5; db/queries.sql Q5; baseline: Commodity cables

question: What exact SFP part numbers are available, with stock and lead time?
reference_sql:
select *
from (
    select distinct on (p.part_id)
           m.name as manufacturer, p.manufacturer_part_number, p.mouser_part_number,
           p.in_stock_qty, p.lead_time_days, h.run_started_at, p.description
    from part_search_hits h
    join search_keywords k using (keyword_id)
    join parts p using (part_id)
    join manufacturers m using (manufacturer_id)
    where k.keyword = 'sfp transceiver'
      and h.run_started_at >= now() - interval '7 days'
    order by p.part_id, h.run_started_at desc
) recent_sfps
order by in_stock_qty desc
correct_behavior: answer: list exact manufacturer and Mouser part numbers with stock and lead time, as of the last sync.

question: Is this cabinet a network rack or a server rack?
reference_sql:
select case when p.description ~* 'network' and p.description ~* 'server' then 'both'
            when p.description ~* 'network' then 'network'
            when p.description ~* 'server' then 'server'
            else 'not stated' end as cabinet_type_in_description,
       count(*) as parts,
       count(*) filter (where p.in_stock_qty > 0) as in_stock
from parts p
where p.category = 'Racks & Rack Cabinets'
group by 1
order by parts desc
correct_behavior: answer_with_caveat: say what the descriptions state, and that there is no cabinet type column, so a part whose description says neither is unknown. Confirm the type with the manufacturer's datasheet.

question: Which SFPs are 25G, or 10/25G auto-sensing?
reference_sql:
select m.name as manufacturer, p.manufacturer_part_number,
       p.description ~* '10\s*/\s*25' as says_10_25,
       p.in_stock_qty, p.lead_time_days, p.description
from parts p
join manufacturers m using (manufacturer_id)
where exists (select 1 from part_search_hits h join search_keywords k using (keyword_id)
              where h.part_id = p.part_id and k.keyword = 'sfp transceiver')
  and p.description ~* '\m25\s*g'
order by says_10_25 desc, p.in_stock_qty desc
correct_behavior: answer_with_caveat: list SFPs whose description says 25G and flag those that say 10/25. Say speed is matched on description text only and auto-sensing is not verified.

question: What will I actually pay after tariffs?
reference_sql:
select p.tariff_pct,
       count(*) as parts,
       round(min(b.unit_price), 2) as lowest_listed,
       round(min(b.unit_price * (1 + p.tariff_pct / 100)), 2) as lowest_with_tariff,
       round(max(b.unit_price), 2) as highest_listed,
       round(max(b.unit_price * (1 + p.tariff_pct / 100)), 2) as highest_with_tariff
from parts p
join lateral (select pb.unit_price from price_breaks pb
              where pb.part_id = p.part_id
              order by pb.quantity limit 1) b on true
where p.tariff_pct is not null
group by p.tariff_pct
order by p.tariff_pct desc
correct_behavior: answer_with_caveat: give the listed price and the price with the quoted tariff. Say Mouser says the tariff 'may be applied', so the final amount is not in the data.

question: How long will an out-of-stock part take to arrive?
reference_sql:
with next_arrival as (
    select part_id, min(expected_date) as next_date
    from part_on_order
    where expected_date >= current_date
    group by part_id
)
select count(*) as out_of_stock,
       count(*) filter (where p.lead_time_days > 0) as lead_time_stated,
       count(*) filter (where p.lead_time_days = 0) as lead_time_not_stated,
       round(avg(p.lead_time_days) filter (where p.lead_time_days > 0)) as avg_stated_lead_days,
       count(n.part_id) as with_on_order_date
from parts p
left join next_arrival n using (part_id)
where p.in_stock_qty = 0
correct_behavior: answer_with_caveat: give the lead time or on-order date where stated. Say a lead time of 0 means not stated, not immediate.

question: What is in stock right now?
reference_sql:
select count(*) filter (where p.in_stock_qty > 0) as parts_in_stock,
       count(*) as parts,
       max(p.data_as_of) as newest_data_as_of,
       (select max(finished_at) from sync_runs where status = 'success') as last_successful_sync,
       now() - (select max(finished_at) from sync_runs where status = 'success') as sync_age
from parts p
correct_behavior: answer_with_caveat: answer as of the last successful sync and give its age. Say the data is not live and stock can change between syncs.
